cards.heading: 1. Prioritize Preventive Screenings and Routine Checkups
title: Where
Preventive Care
Starts
cards.alt: Preventive care starts with a baseline, catches silent markers like blood pressure early, and treats your provider as a partner

items.label: Silent markers
items.note: High blood pressure has no symptoms

items.label: A partnership
items.note: Ask which screenings suit your age

cards.subject: nutrition
cards.heading: 2. Fuel Your Body with Evidence-Based Nutrition
title: Evidence-Based
Nutrition
in Three Parts
cards.alt: Evidence-based nutrition: add fibre-rich plants rather than subtracting, stay hydrated, and cut sugar-sweetened drinks

items.label: Add, don't subtract
items.note: More fibre-rich fruit, veg and whole grains

items.label: Skip sweet drinks
items.note: A major source of added sugar

cards.subject: movement
cards.heading: 3. Move for Longevity, Not Just Fitness
title: Movement
for Longevity
cards.alt: Movement for longevity: 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity weekly, strength work twice a week, and mood benefits

items.label: Mood lift
items.note: Endorphins ease anxiety and low mood

cards.subject: stress
cards.heading: 5. Manage Stress Through Mindful Connection
title: Managing
Stress
Mindfully
cards.alt: Chronic stress causes digestive issues and headaches; breathing, meditation and connection lower cortisol

cards.subject: progesterone
cards.heading: Importance of Progesterone: The Body’s Natural "Peacekeeper"
title: What
Progesterone
Does
cards.alt: Progesterone counterbalances estrogen, is made after ovulation, and converts to a neurosteroid acting on GABA receptors

cards.subject: progesterone
cards.heading: Early Warning Signs: Identifying Hidden Symptoms
title: Early Signs of Low
Progesterone
cards.alt: Low progesterone shows as anxiety, insomnia and irritability, and as heavy bleeding, spotting and shorter cycles

good.heading: Mental and emotional
items: A short fuse, out of character

cards.subject: progesterone
cards.heading: Hidden Impact: Luteal Phase Defects and Hormonal Gaps
title: The Luteal Phase and
Progesterone
cards.alt: A healthy luteal phase runs 12 to 14 days; too little progesterone shortens it, which is a luteal phase defect
cards.gloss: days between ovulation and your period
cards.statLine: the window a healthy luteal phase needs for proper hormonal signalling

cards.subject: progesterone
cards.heading: Fertility Impacts: Thinking About Your Future Family
title: Progesterone
and Fertility
cards.alt: Progesterone ripens the uterine lining, supports implantation, and is measured by tests used to investigate infertility

items.label: Ripens the lining
items.note: So a fertilised egg can implant

items.label: Sustains it
items.note: Too little and the lining breaks down early

cards.subject: progesterone
cards.heading: Restoring Levels: How to Get Your Balance Back
title: Restoring
Progesterone
Levels
cards.alt: Restoring progesterone: magnesium and B6, lowering cortisol, healthy fats for hormone synthesis, and BHRT with testing

cards.subject: birth control
cards.heading: What is Post-Birth Control Syndrome (PBCS)?
title: What Happens After
Birth Control
cards.alt: Hormonal contraceptives suppress the HPO axis; when they stop, the axis comes back online over weeks to months

steps.label: Suppressed
steps.note: Synthetic hormones quiet the HPO axis

steps.label: Removed
steps.note: The body must remember how to produce its own

steps.label: Recalibrating
steps.note: Weeks for some, several months for others

cards.subject: birth control
cards.heading: Common Symptoms Patients Experience
title: Common Symptoms After Stopping
Birth Control
cards.alt: After stopping birth control: cystic acne, libido changes, intense PMS, digestive issues and bloating, hair thinning

cards.subject: birth control
cards.heading: Common Nutrient Depletions Caused by Hormonal Contraceptives
title: Nutrients
Birth Control
Can Deplete
cards.alt: Oral contraceptives can lower B2, B6, B12 and folate, plus magnesium for stress response and zinc for skin

items.label: B vitamins and folate
items.note: B2, B6, B12; B6 builds serotonin and dopamine

items.label: Magnesium
items.note: Regulates the stress response and insulin

cards.subject: birth control
cards.heading: Roadmap to Natural Cycles: Supporting Your Body’s Recovery
title: Recovering Natural Cycles After
Birth Control
cards.alt: Recovery after birth control: healthy fats and protein-first meals, gut health to clear used hormones, and seed cycling

items.label: Gut health
items.note: It clears used hormones, or reabsorbs them

items.label: Seed cycling
items.note: Support for each phase of the cycle
